transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

It is very unlikely to be about to break. Induction hobs work by using magnetic fields that cause the metal in your pan to vibrate at high frequency; this creates a buzzing or humming sound. This effect is much louder with heavy, thick-bottomed stockpots and on higher power settings, so what you are hearing is normal behaviour for an induction hob. You should only be concerned if there are warning signs like a burning smell, sparks, the hob switching off unexpectedly, or loud cracking noises. If it is just the hum while cooking, your hob is working as intended.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

reading.symptom: loud buzzing/humming noise when putting a big stockpot on high heat

plan: They asked: "Is it about to break?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model PUE611BB1E.
The fault they reported is: "loud buzzing/humming noise when putting a big stockpot on high heat". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.
